budgetNotes: budgetMs is a CEILING on p95 at the worst point of the axis — what the engine must not exceed, which is not what it should cost. Derived budgets are 1.5x the measurement; hand-set ones carry a note. Session cases (8 strokes, accumulating) record per-stroke cost and are budgeted on their slowest stroke.

armature_edit.note: PROVISIONAL — hand-set without a device measurement, so this is a ceiling that admits anything reasonable rather than a result. Re-seed with tools/check_device_bench.py <run.json> --update on the reference device and delete this note.

mask_extrude.note: Near linear in document size; would blow this at 10000.

move_drags.note: Timing is not the signal here. Eight drags leave the layer UNRENDERABLE (safe_step_scale 0.003) while each drag stays fast; the gallery's three renders are what carry that, and consolidate is the cure.

pose_region.note: PROVISIONAL — hand-set without a device measurement, so this is a ceiling that admits anything reasonable rather than a result. Re-seed with tools/check_device_bench.py <run.json> --update on the reference device and delete this note.

sdf_consolidate.note: Scales WITH the document (an earlier baseline recorded it flat, from a fixture that re-consolidated an already-consolidated layer).

sdf_stamp_bricks.note: The incremental path, and it is not cheaper than re-evaluating everything. Bricks per stamp is constant across the axis, so the cost is the culled tape compiled per brick — add-item-spatial-index.

sdf_stamp_cpu.note: Already outside the engine's half of a 120 Hz frame (4.17 ms) at 1000 stamps. A regression ceiling on today's behaviour, NOT a claim that it is fast enough; task 8.3 owns recording the size it passes at.

sdf_stamp_metal.note: Metal loses to the CPU at small documents and wins at large. The crossover is the routing rule a host needs.
